verses.text: At night, there on my bed, I looked for the one my soul loves. I looked, but I couldn't find him.
I'll get up and go around the city. I'll look for the one my soul loves in the streets and the squares. I looked, but I couldn't find him.
The guards making their rounds found me. “Have you seen the one my soul loves?”
I'd barely gone past them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and wouldn't let go till I'd brought him into my mother's house, to the room of the woman who conceived me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the does out in the field. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense and all the spices a merchant sells?
Look, it's Solomon's carriage! Sixty mighty men surround it, some of Israel's strongest.
Every one of them can handle a sword and knows how to fight. Each has his sword at his side because of the dangers at night.
King Solomon had a carriage made for himself from wood from Lebanon.
He made its posts silver, its base gold, and its seat purple. The daughters of Jerusalem lined the inside with love.
Come out, daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon wearing the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart was full of joy.
